messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a perf regression on the long-context replay after the kernel selector tweak landed yesterday. p95 jumped and throughput dropped, details below.

dennis: I noticed a blip in the dashboards. Any quick repro steps?

maria: Repro command I used: `./replay_harness --trace replay/2026-03-16 --seq-dist long_prefill_mix --clients 80 --seed 42 --duration 10m` — attached traces and perf counters in the artifact link.

raj: Initial profiling: KV cache miss rate during the prefill window rose from ~8% -> ~26%. CPU/GPU utilization looks similar, but kernel occupancy patterns differ.

olivia: Interesting. Could be the selector misrouting prefill-heavy requests to the non-prefill-optimized kernel. Any kernel logs?

sasha: Hypothesis: kernel selector computes avg_seq based on sample of in-flight tokens (biased by many short inference-only requests), so it picks the fast short-seqlen kernel. But prefill-dominant requests (large max_len/prefill) end up on a kernel with poor KV handling.

dennis: That matches what I saw in the flame graphs — a lot more serialization points in the prefill path. We should pin the selector to the previous policy and do an apples-to-apples run.

maria: Numbers from the failing run (8xA100 pool): p50 +18%, p95 +42%, throughput -22% vs baseline (old selector). I'll attach the flame graphs and event timeline.

ci-bot: perf/regression alert #4332 opened by @maria — https://ci.redwood/perf/4332 (contains traces, artifacts, and baseline comparison).

olivia: Proposal for A2A protocol: 1) take identical replay trace and run N=2 runs with old_selector config, N=2 with new_selector; 2) same cluster size and warmup procedure; 3) capture kernel-selection log, KV metrics, and token-level latency distributions; 4) synthetic long-prefill run with controlled seq-dist as a complement.

raj: For the synthetic suite I recommend seq-dist: 128(20%), 512(20%), 1024(40%), 2048(20%) to approximate our long-prefill mix. Also include a 10k-request prefill-only workload to isolate prefill behavior.

sasha: Add a deterministic KV warmup stage so cache behavior is stable across runs. Example warmup snippet: ```python
# deterministic warmup keys
for i in range(0,200_000):
    client.prefill(key=f\"warm_{i}\", payload=payload_template)
```

dennis: Also enable detailed kernel decision logging: `--kernellog=info --kernellog-file=/tmp/ks.log` so we can see why a kernel was chosen (avglen, maxlen, prefilling flag, model_variant).

maria: Action items (owners):
1) raj: add per-request seqhist and route-by-maxlen guard to selector prototype (branch: sel/route-maxprefill).
2) sasha: add deterministic KV warmup script + include in harness.
3) olivia: run apples-to-apples bench (old vs new selector) with both replay and synthetic suites; upload flamegraphs and kernel logs.
4) dennis: instrument kernel chooser to emit decision reasons and feature stats.

maria: Target: get two full A2A runs and synthetic numbers by EOD tomorrow. If the selector change is root cause we'll revert or gate it behind a prefilling flag.

olivia: Ack :thumbsup: I'll schedule runs on the 8xA100 pool first thing and post links here.

raj: I'll start on the selector patch now, focusing on taking max_prefill_len into the routing score and lowering weight on avglen sampling.

dennis: If we need a quick mitigation, we can fallback to the old kernel for requests with prefilling > 0 until the selector is validated.

maria: Thanks — I'll keep the artifacts and CI links updated in this thread. Please paste any quick numbers here, even small diffs help.

olivia: Uploaded first run artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/4332/run1 (old_selector) and https://ci.redwood/artifacts/4332/run2 (new_selector). Early look: new_selector shows higher prefill-cache churn.

raj: Patch pushed to sel/route-maxprefill, tests passing locally. Will run perf harness once sasha's warmup script is in.

sasha: Warmup script MR: https://git.redwood/infra/warmup/-/merge_requests/215 — includes reproducible keyset and option to prefill only the kv keys used in replay traces.

maria: Good progress. If the A2A shows the selector is the culprit we'll need a changelog and a rollback plan for the production rollout.

dennis: Agreed. Keep CI alert open and add a short hazard note to the deploy runbook.

maria: closing loop — will post final numbers here when done. Thanks everyone.
